### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **61** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-flow-template-paths.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/template.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-flow-template-paths.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/template.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b520c42a2725bdc721d081a4b986aac6bf3273a9` — the merge of head `ef02901d26f2d65d1ce553e99c9cfa42cd9ef871` into base `6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b520c42a2725bdc721d081a4b986aac6bf3273a9 && git checkout b520c42a2725bdc721d081a4b986aac6bf3273a9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672 ef02901d26f2d65d1ce553e99c9cfa42cd9ef871 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672 && git merge --no-ff ef02901d26f2d65d1ce553e99c9cfa42cd9ef871

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c200819d1eca2b4cd7df7dcb13f978793da8495a`
Local-runs: none

PR #22926 (`Part of #19939`, pass 4 stage S4; draft; head repo = base repo; 50 files, +1985 / −350). Read for this record: card #19939's body and all 56 comments — the ruling `6063191653`, the stage plan `6096263424`, the S4 claim `6114980625`, the round-1 report `6117280980`, the seat order `6117306001`, the round-2 report `6118066430`, the ACCEPT `6118088551`, the release `6118101711` and the take-over claim `6118509947` among them — the PR body, its file list, the net diff against `main`, the check-runs on this head, and base files on `origin/main`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`recipients` — right.** Base `z.union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])` becomes a string, a list whose entries are strings or CEL value envelopes, or one envelope (`NotifyRecipientsSlotSchema`, module-local, not exported), with a `superRefine` that refuses a `{…}` token in any string through the one value-slot judge (`valueSlotTemplateRefusals`). Widening: the envelope arms, in the published JSON Schema (`anyOf` string / array / object, pinned) and the inferred `NotifyConfig` type. Narrowing: the token. This is ADR-0032 Decision 2 applied to the highest-pull computed value (census 25 tokens) in S2 and S3's ruled shape. The family finding is fixed by flattening, which the stage plan allowed ("flattened or refused, and pinned"): an entry that evaluates to a list adds each recipient (section 3 of `notify-value-slots.test.ts`); a map, a number or a nested list fails the node naming it, never `String(value)`; `null` and a blank string add none, which keeps the 17.x drop for a token that resolved to nothing, and a node left with none fails naming the sources.
2. **`sourceId` — right.** `z.string()` becomes string or envelope (`NotifySourceIdSlotSchema`, module-local), token refused; the executor requires a string result, `null` leaves the click-through pair unset, anything else fails the node naming what it evaluated to. Widening (the envelope arm, JSON Schema and type) plus narrowing (the token). Census 10.
3. **`templateData` — right.** `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` becomes `z.record(z.string(), FlowValueSlotSchema)`: narrowing only — a `{…}` token in any string at any depth is refused, and an object naming a `dialect` must be a valid CEL envelope. No accept-set widening (an envelope-shaped object was already accepted, as data; it is evaluated now, which the changeset's "Newly accepted" says). The JSON Schema's `additionalProperties` gains the `xExpression: 'value'` marker (pinned).
4. **`actionUrl` — right.** Stays `z.string()`; the contract's `superRefine` refuses a single-brace token through the one text-slot judge, `FLOW_NODE_TEXT_SLOTS` gains `notify.actionUrl` (so `registerFlow`, `objectstack validate` and the executor's `renderTextSlot` all read it), and the two D3 text-slot entries widen their surface to it. Narrowing only. The stage plan's carry line made the link a text slot; a link that renders no text yields to the synthesized one as an empty one did, and an explicit one still wins (pinned).
5. **`sourceObject`, `actorId` — right.** Types unchanged (`z.string()`); a `{…}` token is refused by the contract with the literal remedy and the `readAsWritten` param; an envelope was already refused by the type and now gets the literal's sentence. Narrowing only; no envelope arm, no marker (pinned in the JSON projection). This is the seat order's B (`6117306001`) under the dispatch's Zone 2 item 2, on a zero census here and in hotcrm — and refusing the token rather than forwarding it (the report's option C) is Prime Directive 12's reject-at-authoring, so a picker-written `{record.x}` can never reach the messaging service with its braces.
6. **`payload` — right.** Type unchanged (`z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`); a token in any string at any depth of a value is refused at that string, an envelope written as a value is refused, a deeper envelope stays data. Narrowing only. (The map itself being envelope-shaped is a literal map, read as written — unchanged from 17.x, where nothing evaluated the map either; consistent with "only a slot's top-level value is an expression".)
7. **The build doors' value arm (`flow-node-config-refusals.ts`) — right.** (a) `eachElement`: an issue at a list index is skipped where that element is an envelope (the envelope pass's) or carries a token (the judge's, through the existing token skip), and reported where it is anything else (`42`, `null`, a nested list); an issue at the list itself is skipped only when every element is a string or envelope-shaped, so the union's whole refusal is never reported a second time beside its own judge. Pinned ("the build doors") and ablated (`eachElement` deleted: 5 red). (b) The `READ_AS_WRITTEN_PARAM` short-circuit sits after the region, ledger and run-resolved skips (`RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS` holds `http.signingSecret` only) and before the token skip, so the literal refusals reach `FlowSchema.parse`, `objectstack validate`, the save door, `registerFlow` and the executor's parse — pinned at `FlowSchema.safeParse` and `flowNodeConfigRefusals`, ablated (3 red). `READ_AS_WRITTEN_PARAM` lives in `flow-template-token.ts`, which `automation/index.ts` does not re-export: no new public export, as claimed.
8. **The ledger and the channel — right, with one public type widening to name.** Three `notify` rows are appended at the end of `FLOW_NODE_EXPRESSION_PATHS` (every older row byte-identical, pinned); `recipients` carries the new optional `eachElement` field on the exported `FlowNodeExpressionPath` interface (additive, published through `automation/index.ts`); `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` gains `notify` (its `keyof` widens); the descriptor keeps `recipients` untyped and the other keys unmarked, so one slot has one channel (the ratchet pin) and the Studio form keeps its picker. These additive widenings are covered by the `Clause-②: yes` and the `major`; the arm's prose names only the accept-set widenings — a completeness remark, not a defect.
9. **The executor — right.** `notify-node.ts` no longer imports `interpolate`; `recipients` resolves through `resolveRecipients` over the shared `resolveValueSlot`, `templateData` through `resolveValueSlotMap`, `sourceId` through `resolveStringSlot`, `actionUrl` through `renderTextSlot`, and the literals are read raw. No `??` fallback tolerates an off-spec shape (Prime Directive 12); a token never reaches the executor because the contract parse refuses it first (ablation 1's measured direction). The empty-recipients guard is restated for CEL, naming the sources that evaluated to nothing.
10. **The lint — right, `patch`.** The `flow-double-brace-interpolation` hints name `actionUrl` among the text slots; at a notify literal both wrong-syntax hints name the value itself instead of prescribing `{var}`, which the build now refuses there; `NOTIFY_LITERAL_KEYS` is a local set held equal to the contract by a pin that asks the contract which keys refuse with the literal lead (an export for a hint would widen the spec API). The double-brace control moved from `actionUrl` (a text slot now) to `sourceId`.
11. **ADR-0087 — right.** D3 only: the value-slot entry `flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused` is amended the S1–S3 way (surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria say what a recipient evaluates to, why the list token is not rewritten, and that a literal takes the value itself); the two text-slot entries widen their surface to `actionUrl`; the `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment names the link. No D2: no spelling maps losslessly (an absent variable dropped a recipient and now faults; a list entry reached nobody and now reaches each; a Date in a link renders differently; a record at a recipient became `[object Object]` and now fails the node). No key is removed, so no tombstone.
12. **Sites and generated artifacts — right.** The 41 token strings at the seven positions in the showcase, todo, three docs pages, the README and two dogfood fixtures read 0 at the head; optional recipient fields are guarded (`has(record.assignee) ? record.assignee : null`) and `{$User.Id}` is `current_user != null ? current_user.id : null` (ruling `6063191653`, Q1 A). The showcase `inert-wirings` guard now derives the same three fields from envelope sources (not vacuous). `io-node-config.mdx` is regenerated; `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` moves 708 → 711 with the three new projection-dropped sites. The three private packages touched (`example-showcase`, `example-todo`, `dogfood`) publish nothing.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/19939-flow-notify-value-slots.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **major**, `@objectstack/service-automation` **major**, `@objectstack/lint` **patch**; `.changeset/pre.json` is `mode: pre`, tag `next`, so the release is `18.0.0-next.*`. Right: spec narrows published accept sets on an authoring surface (BREAKING) and widens two; service-automation stops interpolating six positions and evaluates three (a stored flow carrying a token is skipped at boot with a warn); lint changes finding text only, no API. No `skip-changeset`. The FROM → TO table and the one-line fix are present; the title carries `!`.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing: …; widening: …)` — the value `yes` (the envelope arms are newly accepted at `recipients` and `sourceId`), the arm `narrowing` (the token and envelope refusals): S2's ruled shape (`6109208049`), byte-identical on both carriers (the PR body and the changeset, 533 characters). The arm's prose is accurate for every accept-set change in ①; it does not name the additive type widenings of ① item 8, which the value and the `major` already cover.
- ADR-0087 disposition: exactly one marker, `not-required (already-registered …)` naming the three step-18 ids the diff amends; `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Round-1 `open_questions` (the three zero-census keys: value slots or literals) — answered B** by the seat order `6117306001` under the dispatch's Zone 2 item 2, in the non-escalated class with the maintainer's veto window open; round 2 implements all five items of the order (ledger rows out; literal types with the token refusal and remedy; the executor reads raw; the pins; the text that moves — changeset, D3 entry, descriptor, reference, PR body). Round 2 reports `open_questions: []`. Judged right (① items 5 and 6).
- **Dev deviation, `check:type-check-debt` crossed (`--re-measure` plus an unlocked whole-workspace build, both rounds):** a process ⛔, reported by the dev and recorded in the ACCEPT for the seat's stand-down brief; exit 0, no ledger moved; nothing in the diff depends on it. Noted; not a contract matter.
- **Dev deviation, the lint change beyond the order's text list:** judged right — without it the hints would prescribe a spelling the build refuses; `patch` holds.
- **Dev deviation, `origin/main` moved after the round-2 merge:** none of those commits touches a file in this diff; GitHub reads `mergeable: true`; the queue leg merges `main` again.
- **Dev deviation (round 1), the PR assignee written by `label-write --assign` where `os-dev.md` says `pr_create` carries it:** a conflict between two seat texts for the seat to settle; no contract effect.
- **Out-of-scope findings, each with a carrier:** the skill lines `SKILL.md:107/:114/:115/:240` and the class-c CSV-recipient finding → #22585 (the seat); the designer's notify pickers and `FlowRecipientsField`, now including the `:1132` `sourceObject` picker → objectstack-ai/objectui#12101 (the seat); `migrations/entries/README.md:138` naming the removed `check:migration-registry` → an Acceptance note (the seat); the lint's local literal-key set → noted, held by a pin. Each is a note under Prime Directive 10; none buries a defect.
- **Acceptance note, the relation-hop `expand` remedy:** under the template a hop on a scalar id resolved to nothing and the guard named `config.expand`; as a CEL value the hop faults with the key and the source (`recipients[0]: value expression failed to evaluate as CEL: No such key: owner`) and no `expand` hint — the engine's shared value-slot fault since S1, not S4's. Accepted as noted. Recommended for the seat, non-blocking: a pointer on S7 (the engine's canon fixes) or #22585, so the `expand` lesson stays teachable.
